term: factivity of an accepted complete-explanation judgment
definition: For the existing Arrangement arena and independently supplied adequate judgment, AcceptedAreTrue a adequate means every accepted candidate p holds at designated a. This is a substantive OPEN constraint on the judgment, not a definition of truth or actual explanatory adequacy. It is weaker than the existing demand that every accepted candidate select a uniquely. AcceptedFalse is its concrete countercase, while the existing truthful nonselection rival requires p a plus p at a distinct b. Generic judgments can be mistaken; the old explicit false-only control is reused rather than renamed an adequate false explanation. No causal direction, productive explanation, epistemic warrant or applicability to real histories follows.
note: Logic-first scope comparison; no new attribution. Existing mathematical arrangement labels are not automatically real worlds. No transitivity, sufficient causal role or actual empirical truth is introduced by an acceptance predicate. See docs/notes/selection-factivity-coverage.md.
